elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly states: “Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor.
elements.evidence: The added language requires “thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide Customer a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees allocable to the period after the effective date of termination.
elements.evidence: Licensor must “refund to Licensee, pro rata, any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.”

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during any committed term.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “Licensor shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Initial Period or any extension thereof,” covering the initial and extended committed terms.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly grants Licensee a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice period must be between sixty (60) and ninety (90) days.
elements.evidence: The clause provides only thirty (30) days' notice, which is below the fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three (3) months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed for Licensee's exercise of its termination-for-convenience right, so the cap is not exceeded.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only effective at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause prohibits Licensor from terminating for convenience during the Initial Period or an extension, but it does not affirmatively establish a Vendor termination right exercisable only at the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor must provide ninety (90) days' notice to exercise any termination-for-convenience right.
elements.evidence: No ninety-day notice requirement for Licensor is included.

result.reason: The added operative language fully implements the preferred position: Licensee receives a 30-day written-notice convenience right and a pro-rata refund, while Licensor is barred from convenience termination during the initial and extended terms. It does not satisfy the fallback independently because the Customer notice period is not 60–90 days and no end-of-term, 90-day-notice Vendor right is created. The change is limited to the requested termination-for-convenience terms and does not disturb unrelated termination rights.
